posts.text:
It’s going to be a wild week in the US Senate. Buckle up.

I have been calling around to various Republican Senators this weekend.

A few takeaways…

1. Conference is just furious — pissed is an understatement.
2. They see their own inaction on critical issues like the SAVE Act and insider trading bills as a major de-motivator for the midterms. They blame Thune and leadership for playing safe.
3. The rushed Leadership vote Tuesday is seen as a blatant insult. Senators want to know how their Leaders will respond to lame duck session and being in a steep minority. 
4. Over a dozen Senators are demanding round the clock work on Trump nominations and judicial appointments. Some believe parts of the SAVE Act can still be passed through reconciliation.
5. Recess appointments are also being demanded. Thune is holding them up.
6. Senators are openly questioning their adherence to “tradition” — blue slip, filibuster etc. — as a new crop of Democrats couldn’t care less and will destroy tradition for power in a heartbeat.
7. There’s a sense that something big is going to happen. A real shakeup. Stay tuned…

One Senator tells me: “The guys blocking an America First conference are all gone now. It’s never going back to the old ways. Time to try new things…”

Buckle up.

posts.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump may be preparing another MAJOR ATTACK on Iran, even as JD Vance tries to END THE WAR

Brandon Weichert spoke with Andrew Day, senior editor of The American Conservative, as fresh American strikes were being reported on Iran's Qeshm Island.

And Andrew sees some troubling similarities to the buildup before the February 28 war.

American military transport flights are increasing around Diego Garcia, Patriot air defenses are being repositioned, and as many as THREE US aircraft carriers could be operating in the region by mid-to-late November.

None of that proves Trump has decided to attack.

But Andrew warned that Washington may be assembling the military capabilities for another major offensive while diplomacy continues in the background.

There's another danger: CENTCOM's expanding pressure campaign against Iran's land routes and Caspian Sea trade could bring American forces into confrontation with Russian-linked shipping.

Two wars that Washington has struggled to contain could become dangerously connected.

We also discussed what Trump's midterm defeat means for his next move.

Andrew doesn't believe the election necessarily made Trump more cautious. He thinks the president could also be tempted to retaliate against Iran for the political damage the war has inflicted.

And there's a deadline worth watching.

December 11.

That's when Congress faces a government funding deadline, potentially giving Democrats leverage to restrict further spending on the Iran war.

But Andrew's preferred solution is considerably simpler than the comprehensive nuclear agreement Trump keeps demanding.

Stabilize the ceasefire, reach a limited arrangement over the Strait of Hormuz and withdraw American forces from Iran's immediate vicinity.

Trump doesn't need a grand bargain to end this war. He needs to stop treating another bombing campaign as the alternative.

@WeTheBrandon @AKDay89
